answer: The submission is honest and well-scoped, but it reads as a concept plus early pilot rather than a validated venture. Priority improvements: (1) Strengthen traction evidence. Report trial usage metrics (sessions per vendor per week, days recorded, retention after 2-4 weeks), conversion intent from the 12 trial users, and why the one payer converted. One paying customer at $27 total is thin; showing behavioral evidence matters more than the interview counts. (2) Fix the market math. The top-down 85,000 figure is acknowledged as unvalidated; replace or supplement it with a bottom-up build from the 1,200 local vendors, and cite a source for vendor counts. Note the revenue arithmetic is internally consistent (180 x $9 x 12 = about $19,400) but a 15% paid conversion is an unsupported assumption, and at the stated 180-vendor ceiling the local opportunity is too small to sustain a business, so explain the path from local ARR to a venture-scale or at least sustainable outcome. Also reconcile the 100-paying-vendor 12-month projection with the 180-vendor local scenario so the numbers tell one story. (3) Sharpen competitive differentiation. The plan admits competitors have offline modes, tax features, and card payments. Name specific competitors (e.g., Square, Shopify POS, QuickBooks, market-specific tools), compare features in a table, and explain concretely why vendors would switch. Leading with 'simpler' is weak without evidence, such as time-to-first-sale or vendor quotes. Card payments being absent is a major gap since many vendors already take cards through another processor; clarify how Ledgerleaf coexists with those tools (e.g., manual card tagging, reconciliation against processor reports) and whether the $3,500 integration budget is realistic. (4) Add unit economics and pricing logic. Estimate CAC from the pilot (time and travel per onboarded vendor), expected churn given seasonality, and lifetime value. Address directly the seasonality problem the team itself flags: annual plans, seasonal pausing, or pricing tied to market days. Justify $9 against vendor margins and the cost of the problem (hours saved, tax errors avoided), and consider quantifying that cost, since the problem section calls it small per day. (5) Tighten claims about the problem. Twelve of 23 'unsure at some point' about tax is anecdotal; clarify how interviews were conducted, avoid leading questions, and note sampling limits (three nearby markets). Include one or two direct quotes and what vendors currently pay for tools. (6) Clarify the market-manager revenue idea or cut it. Untested and potentially in tension with vendor trust and data privacy; either run a few manager conversations or remove it from the model. (7) Address risk and compliance. Tax rates vary by jurisdiction and product type (many farm products are exempt); explain how the app handles exemptions, rate changes, and liability disclaimers, since incorrect tax estimates are a core trust risk. Also cover data security of financial records. (8) Make the use of funds measurable. Tie each budget line to a milestone and success threshold (e.g., X paid vendors across 10 markets, Y% 60-day retention, CAC under Z). Justify why $4,000 for legal/accounting setup is the right amount, and consider whether $15,000 with 45 hours/week of combined founder time is enough to hit the goals; state a timeline with dated milestones. (9) Address team capacity and gaps. All three are full-time students at 15 hours/week; explain commitment after graduation, who owns sales and market relationships, and what happens if the CTO is a single point of failure. Note that the mentorship asks are good but should be prioritized by what decisions they would unlock. (10) Presentation: add a short 'key assumptions and how we will test them' section, a one-line vision beyond the pilot, a simple screenshot or workflow description, and consistently quantify claims. Trim hedging language where evidence exists and keep it only where it truly does not. Overall, the biggest lift would come from replacing assumptions with measured pilot data and a clear, falsifiable plan for the next 6-12 months.
